thread.title: Here are the national, North Texas stocks getting pummeled in the market rout

author: Jon Prior
title: Here are the national, North Texas stocks getting pummeled in the market rout
text: – Dallas Business Journal Feb 6, 2018, 2:37pm CST Stock markets appeared to rebound today following a record-setting selloff Feb. 5 that sent shockwaves throughout the U.S. economy. After rebounding from early losses this morning, major stock indices have shot back into positive territory during late-day trading. Wall Street experts said the broader declines, which began in earnest Jan. 29, might be driven by investor worries that the economy is entering a period of steeper than normal inflation. The recent losses have been widespread and industry agnostic. Among the biggest losers as of Monday was Seattle-based radio technology and software maker Impinj Inc. (Nasdaq: PI), which saw its stock price plummet 45 percent to $11.94 between Jan. 29 and Feb. 5. Other companies that took double-digit hits to their stock prices included Overstock.com (Nasdaq: OSTK), down 36 percent to $49.50; Eastman Kodak Co. (NYSE: KODK) down 35 percent to $6.20; and Bellicum Pharmaceuticals (Nasdaq: BLCM) down 35 percent to $5.61. The largest wealth managers in Dallas aren't panicking about the the topsy-turvy moves in stocks recently. "Corrections are normal and this one has been a long time in the making," said Rick Szelc , managing director for Dallas wealth management firms Neuberger Berman. Szelc added that the market's volatility has been dormant for the last year by historical standards and is actually creating an opportunity. "Volatility in markets is normal," Szelc said. More problematic signs that the market is anticipating a more drastic economic slowdown - like a drop in consumer confidence or widening credit spreads on certain debt - hasn't happened yet, Szelc said. "We believe this rise in rates caused the initial stock sell-off and the late day acceleration was likely momentum driven and our belief is that US and global growth will remain strong over the intermediate term and equity markets will stabilize and move higher," said David Adamson, director of investments at Dallas-based Weilert Wunderlick Armstrong's wealth strategy group. Dhruv Maniktala, director of global investment strategy at one Dallas' largest wealth managers, True North Advisors , said they have been worried about overvalued stocks for three years, but the decline in share prices over the past 10 days only took the market back to where it was in early December. They have been putting their clients' portfolios in a defensive position over the past couple of years and are in the middle of making more changes amidst the volatility. "We have a strong belief that bad things happen to overvalued markets, and as such, were not surprised by the recent events," Maniktala said. The slide follows a stretch that saw U.S. stocks hit historic highs amid investor excitement over strong corporate earnings reports, a growing economy and the passage of a business-friendly tax bill. Last month, the stalwart Dow Jones Industrial Average took just seven days to add 1,000 points and surpass 26,000 for the first time in its history. The Nasdaq and S&P 500 also set new records in the early days of 2018. Markets took a sharp turn last week, and the declines accelerated through Monday, with the Dow tumbling to a low of 24,085 as of today's opening bell. Gina Martin Adams , chief equity strategist for Bloomberg Intelligence, said investors were overly optimistic in 2017 amid a steady stream of strong corporate earnings reports. But a number of sectors have been rocked by developments that created something of a contagion effect heading into this week's selloff, Adams said. For example, health care stocks spiraled in the wake of the joint announcement by Amazon (Nasdaq: AMZN), Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRK.A) and JPMorgan Chase (NYSEL: JPM) of plans to create a joint health care venture aimed at reducing health care costs for employees. Similar reverberations hit the tech sector with Apple’s (Nasdaq: AAPL) introduction of an update to its health app that will enable customers to view medical records on their phones. Add in disappointing earnings reports from ExxonMobil (NYSE: XOM) and Chevron (NYSE: CVX), and some investors are feeling the heat, spurring fears that ultimately rippled through the broader market, Adams said. “There were some pretty big losses in some specialized products,” Adams said. “It seems to be a symptom of a deflation of the excess of investor optimism." “It’s still a bull market,” Adams said. “As long as the fundamentals of the market are strong, which they are, I don’t see that changing.”
